key_insight: Single-qubit re-uploading circuits can match the expressive power of multi-qubit circuits with the same encoding budget, but they are much harder to train by first-order methods because their parameters become phase-locked on the Bloch sphere.
engineering_relevance: For quantum model design, this shows that trading qubit width for circuit depth may preserve function class but can sharply reduce optimization reliability and training efficiency.
method: Compare serial single-qubit and two-qubit control circuits under the same encoding budget E.
Analyze tangent directions and Fourier-coefficient capacity to explain the phase-locking effect.
Evaluate convergence on synthetic flat-spectrum targets and three real-world time series using gradient descent, Adam, and Levenberg-Marquardt.
evidence_signal: At E=32 on the exact-loss benchmark, the serial circuit converged in 3, 53, and 83 runs for gradient descent, Adam, and Levenberg-Marquardt, while the two-qubit control converged in 99, 100, and 100 runs; on real series, the control also reached the optimum far more often and usually achieved lower test error.
watch_item: The results depend on first-order training dynamics and matched parameter-count comparisons, so practical performance may vary with initialization, optimizer settings, and hardware noise.
paper_title: Same Spectrum, Harder First-Order Training: Phase-Locking in Single- versus Multi-Qubit Re-Uploading Circuits
